section.sectionSummaryBrief: The three aspects of Yaakov's journey are present in every Jew, as the deeds of the fathers empower the children, especially regarding Yaakov.
section.t: Now, the three above-mentioned matters that were in Yaakov –
his departure from Be'er Sheva to Charan,
his service
(after the departure from Be'er Sheva)
"And he took from the stones of the place, etc.,"
(that through his prayer)
this stone
(which he took from the stones of the place)
became the house of G-d – exist also in each and every Jew.
For "the deeds of the fathers are a sign and give power to the children"
(as above, section 2),
and especially the matters of Yaakov.
For since "the beauty of Yaakov is like the beauty of Adam HaRishon,"
and his soul includes all the souls of Israel
(like the soul of Adam HaRishon),
therefore the service of Yaakov
("And he took from the stones of the place, etc.")
gives power to the children with greater excellence and greater strength.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: The departure of the soul from its lofty source to the body is empowered by an oath to be righteous, enabling its service below.
section.t: The explanation is,
that "And Yaakov departed from Be'er Sheva and went to Charan" refers
to the descent of the soul into the body,
that it descended from a high
peak
(Be'er Sheva)
to a deep pit
(Charan).
And just as Yaakov,
in order to be able to go to Charan, was drawn a more elevated power – the matter of "Command the salvations of Yaakov"
(as above, section 5),
so too is it regarding the "and he went to Charan" in each and every Jew,
that before the descent of the soul below into the deep pit,
which is the matter of "and he went to Charan,"
they give it a special power so that it can perform its service of refining the body, the animal soul, and its portion in the world.
And as is known
regarding the matter of "they adjure him: 'Be righteous and do not be wicked.'"
And this is the meaning of "And Yaakov departed from Be'er Sheva, etc.,"
that the explanation of "Be'er Sheva" is
that which they adjure him: "Be righteous, etc."
[There are three explanations of this:
an oath,
satiety and seven,
as explained in many places]
which is a special empowerment for the service of the soul in its descent below.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: The soul's service below consists of Torah and mitzvos, which elevate it, and the refinement of the body and animal soul through all one's actions being for G-d's sake.
section.t: Now, the service of the soul in its descent below is
(generally)
in two matters.
First,
the study of Torah and the fulfillment of the mitzvos,
for specifically through the study of Torah and fulfillment of the mitzvos below, the soul is elevated higher than it was before its descent.
And as is known,
the Torah and mitzvos specifically below become a garment for the soul in the Garden of Eden, through which it apprehends and delights in the Ein Sof.
And second,
the refinement of the body, the animal soul, and its portion in the world.
This is accomplished through the fulfillment of the mitzvos,
and even more so – through the service of "all your deeds shall be for the sake of Heaven,"
and especially through "in all your ways know Him,"
that not only should his permissible actions be for the sake of Heaven,
but that even in them themselves
(in all your ways)
there should be "know Him"
[knowledge of G-dliness,
for "knowledge" is higher even than wisdom,
as explained at length in the continuation of the discourse of the Tzemach Tzedek
and in many places].
And this is "and He will give me bread to eat and a garment to wear, and I will return in peace to my father's house,"
"bread to eat and a garment to wear" refers to the study of Torah and the fulfillment of the mitzvos,
as is known,
that Torah is bread and food for the soul, and the mitzvos are garments for the soul,
and "I will return in peace" is the matter of the work of refinement.
